title: Millet: Protein, Carbohydrates, and Minerals

seo.title: Millet: Protein, Carbohydrates, and Minerals
seo.meta_description: Cooked millet provides about 119 calories, 3.5 g protein, and 24 g carbohydrate per 100 g, plus magnesium and phosphorus.
seo.search_intent: Understand millet nutrition and how it compares with other grains.

excerpt: Millet is a naturally gluten-free cereal that, cooked, provides roughly 119 calories, 3.5 g protein, and 24 g carbohydrate per 100 g. Its cooked fiber content is modest, while dry millet contributes minerals including magnesium, phosphorus, and manganese.
content_html:
Millet is not one single species but a group of small-seeded cereal grains eaten around the world. Nutritionally it behaves more like rice or couscous than like a legume: carbohydrate is the dominant macronutrient.

What cooked millet provides

A common USDA reference is about 119 calories, 3.5 g protein, 24 g carbohydrate, and roughly 1–1.5 g fiber per 100 g cooked.

That is useful grain nutrition, but not an unusually high protein amount.

Minerals

Dry millet contributes magnesium, phosphorus, manganese, and copper. Cooking water lowers the concentration per 100 g, as with other grains.

Naturally gluten-free

Millet is naturally gluten-free. People with celiac disease should still manage cross-contact in processed products.

Texture changes with water

Less water gives a fluffier grain; more water and longer cooking produces a creamy, polenta-like texture.

Millet’s main value is grain variety, not a spectacular single nutrient number.

faq.question: How much protein is in cooked millet?
Is millet low-carb?
faq.answer: No. Cooked millet contains roughly 24 g carbohydrate per 100 g.
